case_number: Criminal Petitions No.176-K to 179-K of 2022 and 1493 of 2022
related_cases: High Court of Sindh Judgment dated 14-10-2022
Special Criminal A.T. Appeals No.168, 169, 170, 171 and 173 of 2021

facts.location: Lane-5 near Castle Lights, Bukhari Commercial, Phase-V, DHA Karachi
facts.summary: Police officials opened fire at the vehicle of Intezar Ahmed during patrol duty after he allegedly failed to stop. The firing resulted in his death. The prosecution alleged intentional murder, while the defence claimed the act occurred during discharge of official duty without ill will.

forensic_reports: FSL ballistic report confirming empties matched with pistols of Muhammad Daniyal and Bilal Rasheed

legal_issues.finding: When accused are police officials and investigation is conducted by same force, strict standards may not apply due to possibility of deliberate concessions.
Court adopted third view that petitioners fired in purported discharge of duty but exceeded authority.
Petitioners exceeded powers in good faith without ill will; case falls under Exception 3 to old Section 300 PPC; conviction altered to Section 302(c) PPC.
No sufficient grounds to interfere with acquittal recorded by High Court.

respondent: FSL report conclusively connects weapons to crime empties.

judgment_summary.Criminal Petitions No.176-K to 179-K of: Converted into appeal; conviction under Section 302(b) PPC converted to Section 302(c) PPC; sentence reduced to 15 years imprisonment; remaining convictions maintained; benefit of Section 382-B Cr.P.C extended

legal_references.case_name: Syed Ali Bepari v. Nibaran Mollah and others
Ali Muhammad v. Ali Muhammad and another

remarks: Supreme Court held that petitioners, as public servants, exceeded authority in good faith without ill will. Conviction altered to Section 302(c) PPC and sentence reduced to 15 years imprisonment.
